articles.summary: STORY: From Nvidia drumming up cash to four legged robots keeping homes safe. This is Tech Weekly. :: Tech Weekly Nvidia said it's partnered with six major financial institutions to launch compute financing platforms... aimed at raising over $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said on X that the company has the option to backstop up to $125 billion, or 25% of the potential deals. The move highlights how surging demand for AI computing capacity is drawing institutional investors. A U.S. appeals court allowed thousands of lawsuits to move forward against Meta Platforms, Alphabet's Google, ByteDance's TikTok and Snap Inc's Snapchat. It's over claims they designed their products to be addictive to young users. A San Francisco-based court rejected an appeal by Meta and TikTok seeking to overturn a lower court ruling requiring them to face more than 3,000 lawsuits filed in federal court. Eyewitness video captured the moment China’s Long March 7A rocket exploded after take-off in Hainan. State news agency Xinhua said the cause was under investigation. The failure could trigger checks of other Chinese launches if investigators identify a problem involving shared components, manufacturing or Wenchang launch operations. And would you trust a robot dog to keep you safe at home? "Hey this is Landon from Undaunted products. How can I help you today?" Robotic dogs are replacing overnight security guards at several Atlanta apartment complexes, where property managers say the machines are helping deter crime and improve safety. At 445 Cleveland Apartments, two four-legged robots patrol the property's roughly 200 units. The robots, operated by Atlanta-based startup Undaunted, are remotely controlled by human operators. They monitor live camera feeds and communicate directly with residents through onboard speakers.
